messages.subject: Proposal ranking and "ignored".
parts:
There have been several queries to the admins about projects being marked "ignored".

Here is some information that may put this in context.

1) We got about 60 proposals this year, up 50% from last year.

2) We were tentatively allocated 16 slots for funding, up 1 from last year.

3) Google insists on announcing the proposals and students who got funded -- we therefore
won't answer whether a project is or is not accepted or rejected.

4) Students can only be funded for 1 project.

5) We have therefore asked students with more than one proposal to indicate which they
would like to have considered, and to withdraw the other(s).

6) In general, only one student is funded per project idea. Where there are multiples we
have to sometimes make a painful choice, especially when some proposals that are not
number 1 in a popular topic are clearly better than the number 1 for another topic.

7) With so many proposals to consider, it is sometimes helpful to "ignore" some proposals
for a while as we rank others. They can be "unignored" again if the admins choose.

After Google makes the announcements, it would be helpful if mentors would provide
feedback to those students who clearly did a reasonable job but were not successful. We
want to enlarge our developer community and bring new energy and ideas to R. As for the
spammy proposals -- we hope they will please find more productive things to do.

JN
